help_title: In the browser or in the terminal.
help_lead: The same idea in both: few decisions, explicit checks and clear results. These are the real jgates commands.
help_copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the command and copy it by hand.
help_step_init_text: Creates jgates.yml and the .jgates files from the languages the project uses.
help_step_ui_text: Configure templates, review the plan and follow the runs in a local interface that only serves your computer.
help_step_plan_text: Shows the plan before running any tool: what runs, what does not apply and what was left without coverage.
help_step_run_text: Runs exactly the plan and returns structured output, with the exit code the pipeline can use.
help_more_history: Lists the runs of this workspace.
help_more_baseline: Marks a run as the baseline to compare the next ones.
help_more_gc: Shows what retention would delete, without deleting anything.
help_more_doctor: Checks the runtimes and tools of the machine.
help_more_update: Checks whether a newer JGates is available and, if you confirm, installs it. Only goes online when you run it.
help_more_no_cache: Runs everything again, without reusing results from earlier runs.
help_more_waiver: Waives a finding in the project, with a reason and an end date: use Waive on a finding of the result, or the terminal. The run then says approved with N waivers.
help_more_no_waivers: Runs accepting no waiver at all, for a deploy flow: the findings count as they are.
help_more_coverage: Shows every OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 requirement in one of five states, from what your validations really ran: examined, unexamined, unsupported, not applicable and awaiting evidence. It shows what was examined, not whether the project meets the standard.
help_more_preserve: Protects a run from retention cleanup.
help_faq_profile_q: What is the difference between profile and severity?
help_faq_profile_a: The profile sets the depth and cost of the checks. Severity sets which results block delivery. A fast profile can still block an exposed secret.
help_faq_architecture_q: Does JGates discover the right architecture by itself?
help_faq_architecture_a: It identifies files, languages and dependencies. The desired architecture is declared by you, in .jgates/architecture.yml: layers, limits and contracts that must be preserved.
help_faq_cache_q: Why did a result come back reused?
help_faq_cache_a: If nothing the check reads has changed, the result of an earlier run is reused, and the result says which run it came from. Use --no-cache to run everything again.
help_faq_waiver_a: It takes one finding out of blocking, with a reason and an end date, and is saved in .jgates/waivers.json of the project (Waive on the result, or jgates waivers add). A run that passes with waivers says approved with N waivers; jgates run --no-waivers accepts none. It never turns a check that failed into approved: if the check errored, the run stays unapproved. A waiver that is expired or no longer matches the code does not apply.
help_faq_asvs_q: What does the ASVS coverage map tell me?
help_faq_asvs_a: For the level you choose, each requirement is examined (a check tied to it ran to completion), unexamined (it could run and did not, with the reason), unsupported (no JGates check is mapped to it), not applicable (you recorded that, with a reason, in .jgates/asvs.json) or awaiting evidence (it needs a deployed system or a person). Examined means a check looked for violations of part of the requirement, not that the requirement is met; each row says what the check covers and misses. Semgrep rules count only when the Semgrep check ran and scanned a file of the rule's language, and a Semantic audit counts apart, as an AI review of the source. The requirement text is the official OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, © The OWASP Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. See docs/jgates/asvs-coverage.en.md.
help_faq_governed_a: The policy comes from outside the repository and governed fields appear locked, with the reason. The interface does not loosen what the policy requires.
help_keyboard_q: How do I use it with the keyboard only?
help_keyboard_a: Use Tab to navigate, Enter or Space to activate controls, Esc to close dialogs and the arrow keys to switch tabs. In the editor, Tab inserts two spaces; Esc moves focus out of the editor.
help_more_asvs_review: Asks an AI to review the source against the ASVS requirements that no deterministic check examined. It needs a finished validation, shows the number of requirements and the cost before it starts, and its answers are shown apart as an AI review of the source.
